content:
I recently discovered a significant performance issue in my (WSL) Lean setup that was caused by the 'GitHub Pull Requests' vscode extension. The problem is that when I opened vscode, with at least one Lean file open, a Lean process was started for every single file touched by the current PR. I discovered this while working on #39433, which touches 17 files. In particular, I used the command ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -30 to see all these Lean processes that suddenly appeared, and then disappeared again a bit later, using up a significant amount of available CPU while they were active.

I've seen earlier discussion of performance problems of this extension, but I think this is different from the previously observed problem, so I thought it might be worth sharing (#lean4 > Many Lean processes on Windows ).

(I've now uninstalled the extensions, and after a lot of effort I made a shell script that imitates what the extension provides)

It's unfortunately not too likely that they'll fix this issue, since they also closed our previous issue without even really trying to reproduce it.

We'll hopefully be able to mitigate this particular issue once Microsoft releases the next version of the language client library. Sadly that too has been stalled for years at this point.
Cross-referencing #general > PR review tooling idea @ 💬, where @Floris van Doorn mentioned the same issue.
I have been reluctant to install that extension, but the behaviour it enables sounds pretty nice. Would you like to share your shell script/how your workflow looks like? (Another thread is fine!)
Perhaps if a bunch of people upvote the issue we can ping on that closed issue?
